No mathematical content: this is the structure projection pulling the additivity-in-the-first-argument axiom field out of the `InnerProductSpace` class.
Not a proof: this is the projection of the `add_left` axiom field out of the InnerProductSpace class (additivity of the inner product in the first slot is an assumed axiom). No step to explain.
Auto-generated field accessor of the BindStruct structure: the conclusion is literally one of the structure's fields, so the proof is the projection. No mathematics.
This is an auto-generated field accessor of a structure — the 'proof' is the projection itself. There is no mathematical step; the only thing worth naming is the structure being projected.
This is an auto-generated structure field accessor for BindStruct; the 'proof' is the projection itself, with no mathematical step at all.

`IsBimonHom` is declared as a class extending `IsMonHom` and `IsComonHom`, so this is the auto-generated parent projection: extract the monoid-hom half of a bimonoid-hom instance. There is no argument, only field access.

A pure parent-structure projection: `IsBimonHom` is declared as extending the monoid-hom condition, so this 'proof' is the auto-generated field access. There is no mathematical step at all; the content is unnameable by any citation.

This is the auto-generated parent projection of a class that extends two others: a bimonoid morphism is in particular a monoid morphism. The 'proof' is the structure field access, carrying no mathematical step.
Unfold cancellability of 0 to the implication 0 + a ≤ 0 + b → a ≤ b, rewrite zero_add on both sides, and the remaining implication is literally the identity function.
Rewrite 0 + a to a on both sides using zero_add, after which the goal a ≤ b → a ≤ b is discharged by the identity function.

To show 0 is additively cancellable for ≤: rewrite 0 + a and 0 + b down to a and b using zero_add, after which the required implication is the identity. One real lemma (zero_add) plus the identity function; everything else is simp's congruence scaffolding.

The identity morphism of a frame object is the identity frame hom, so applying it to x returns x; simp unfolds the bundled identity and closes by reflexivity. The content is definitional unfolding, not any citable lemma — and the unfolding lemmas themselves are not in the list.

The identity morphism of a frame is the identity frame hom, which acts as the identity function, so applying it to x returns x; `simp` closes it via the hom_id simp lemma. The candidate list contains only simp's closing residue and ambient types, not the lemma that does the work.

The identity morphism of a frame object has underlying frame hom the identity, which applied to x gives x; closed by simp. The genuinely used facts are the hom_id lemma and the identity-application lemma, neither of which appears here — the listed items are simp's `of_eq_true`/`eq_self` residue.
Not a proof: the structure projection extracting the `property` field from an InducedWideCategory morphism, i.e. by construction such a morphism carries a proof that it satisfies P.
No mathematical content: the structure projection extracting the `property` field (the proof that the underlying morphism satisfies P) from a morphism of the induced wide category.
Not a proof: the projection extracting the `property` field from the Hom structure of an induced wide category (a morphism there is by construction a morphism of D satisfying P). Nothing to argue.

A simps-generated component lemma for the counit isomorphism of the shuffle equivalence prodμ on product categories: unfold the composite of associators and braidings componentwise and cancel identity compositions. Real content is pure normalisation, not a cited theorem; the only named idea used is comp_id.

An auto-generated projection lemma for the counit isomorphism of the equivalence prodμ (built from associators and a braiding on product categories). The proof just unfolds the composite equivalence componentwise and cancels identity compositions; everything else is simp's congruence/transitivity residue.

A `simps`-generated component lemma for the counit inverse of an equivalence built by composing associators and a braiding. The proof is mechanical: unfold the composite, observe every component is an identity morphism in the product category, and collapse the identity compositions. No mathematical idea beyond `comp_id`.

The unit map of a commutative group object is unchanged by the forgetful functor to group objects. Since forget₂Grp is the induced functor along CommGrp.toGrp, both sides are the same term and the proof is rfl — definitional transparency of an induced-category functor is the whole content.

Purely definitional: the forgetful functor from commutative groups to groups leaves the underlying object and its monoid unit untouched, so the unit of the image is literally the same morphism. Closed by rfl.

Pure reflexivity. The forgetful functor from commutative group objects to group objects is an induced functor, so the underlying object and hence its unit map are definitionally unchanged; there is no argument beyond unfolding.

The numeral `ofNat(a)` in a matrix ring is the Nat-cast, which is a diagonal matrix; so the statement is an instance of the already-proved fact that the Hadamard product of an adjacency matrix with any diagonal matrix is zero (the adjacency matrix vanishes on the diagonal). One-line specialisation.

A numeral matrix (Nat.cast/OfNat) is a scalar, hence diagonal, matrix, and the Hadamard product of an adjacency matrix with a diagonal matrix vanishes because the adjacency matrix is zero on the diagonal; so the statement is an instance of the diagonal version.

An OfNat numeral at a matrix type is a diagonal (scalar) matrix, and the adjacency matrix has zero diagonal, so this is a direct instance of the general Hadamard-with-a-diagonal-matrix-is-zero lemma. No new content.
Direct application of the general joint-surjectivity statement for colimit cocones in Type: every point of the colimit is hit by some component of the cocone.
Specialize the general statement (that the cocone maps into a colimit in Type are jointly surjective) from an abstract IsColimit witness to the chosen colimit cocone; a single application.
Specialize the general statement about arbitrary colimit cocones in Type to the chosen colimit cocone: every element of the colimit is in the image of some component map. A single application.

A `rfl` simp-lemma: the underlying map of the order isomorphism `mapAddSubgroup` induced by an additive equivalence is by construction the pushforward of subgroups, so the coercion computes definitionally.

The underlying set of the order-isomorphism image of an additive subgroup is by construction the image, so the coercion lemma is true by definition and closes with rfl. The only real ingredient is how mapAddSubgroup was defined.
The underlying set of the order isomorphism on subgroups induced by an additive equivalence is by construction the image map, so the coercion lemma is true by definition (rfl).

Definitional unfolding (rfl): the underlying natural transformation of the identity morphism in the category of lax monoidal functors is the identity of the underlying functor, which holds by construction of that category instance.
The underlying functor morphism of the identity morphism of a lax monoidal functor is the identity; holds by definition of the category structure, proved by rfl.
The underlying natural transformation of the identity morphism of a lax monoidal functor is the identity of the underlying functor, true by construction of the category instance; reflexivity.

Definitional unfolding (rfl): the counit isomorphism of the equivalence of discrete categories induced by an equivalence of types is the isomorphism built from the type-level round trip. Reading off the definition, nothing proved.
Projection lemma naming the counit isomorphism of the equivalence of discrete categories induced by an equivalence of types; definitional, closed by rfl.
Projection lemma: the counit iso of the equivalence of discrete categories induced by an equivalence of types is the one written in the definition, so reflexivity closes it.
Definitional unfolding (rfl): the hom component of the isomorphism of frames built from an order isomorphism is the underlying order map. No content beyond reading the constructor.
Projection lemma: the hom component of an isomorphism of frames built from an order isomorphism is the underlying order map; definitional, proved by rfl.
Projection lemma for the constructor of an iso in the category of frames built from an order iso: the hom component is by construction the underlying order map, so reflexivity closes it.
Integer strict inequality a < x unfolds to a + 1 ≤ x, so the statement is exactly the non-strict le_min characterization applied at a + 1. The successor shift is the whole idea.
Use that a < b is a + 1 ≤ b over the integers, so the strict version of 'less than a min' is exactly the non-strict lemma applied at a + 1.

Use that on the integers a < b is definitionally a + 1 <= b, so the strict version of 'below the min iff below both' is exactly the non-strict lemma applied at a + 1. The successor shift is the whole idea.

Definitional unfolding (rfl): the unit morphism of the monoidal structure on the inverse of the double-monoidal-opposite equivalence is the identity after stripping two unmop's. No mathematical step beyond unfolding.
Projection lemma reading off the unit-comparison morphism η of the monoidal structure on the inverse of the mop-mop equivalence; true by definition, proved by rfl.
A projection lemma for the monoidal structure on the double-monoidal-opposite equivalence: the unit morphism eta unwraps to the identity by definition, so the proof is reflexivity.
A one-line specialization: instantiate the general 'n is congruent to its digit sum mod b' lemma at base 10 and modulus 3, and discharge the numeric side condition 10 ≡ 1 (mod 3) by computation.

Specialises the general 'n is congruent to its digit sum mod b when the base is 1 mod b' lemma to base 10 and modulus 3, discharging the numeric side condition 10 % 3 = 1 by computation. The only real step is picking the instantiation.

A number is congruent mod 3 to the sum of its base-3 digits. This is the b = b' = 3 case of the general digit-sum congruence lemma; the only work is instantiating it and discharging the trivial numeric side condition.

Pure definitional unfolding (rfl): the functor from coalgebras of the product comonad to the over-category sends a coalgebra map to the same underlying morphism, and its structure map is the coalgebra map followed by the first projection. Nothing is proved beyond reading off the definition.
A simp-lemma unfolding the action of the coalgebra-to-over-object functor on morphisms; it holds by definition, so the proof is reflexivity. No mathematical step beyond unfolding the construction.

An auto-generated projection lemma: the action of the coalgebra-to-over-category functor on morphisms is literally what the definition writes down, so the proof is reflexivity. No mathematical step at all.
Re-exposes the triangle inequality that is already a field of the SeminormedSpace.Core structure. The proof is a structure projection applied to the given Core instance; no argument is made.

Extracts the triangle inequality from the SeminormedSpace.Core structure: the field is literally one of the axioms bundled in Core, so the proof is a projection out of the given structure. No real mathematical step beyond naming the axiom.
The triangle inequality for a seminormed-space Core is just the corresponding field of the Core structure; the proof projects that field out. No mathematical step beyond structure projection.

Finset.sup is implemented as a fold of the join over the finset starting at bottom; since join is idempotent (and commutative/associative), the fold-over-insert lemma for idempotent operations gives the result directly, with no case analysis on whether the inserted element was already present.
`Finset.sup` is a fold of `max` starting at ⊥; since max is idempotent, the fold-over-insert lemma applies without needing a ∉ s, giving f a ⊔ s.sup f directly.
Finset.sup is a fold of the binary sup starting at bottom; since sup is idempotent (and commutative/associative), inserting an element just joins its value on, which is exactly fold_insert_idem.

The single function is the zero function updated at one coordinate, so the statement is the already-proved image formula for Function.update applied with the base point zero; the proof is that specialization.

`Pi.single i a` is `Function.update 0 i a`, so the image of a single-coordinate Ico is exactly the specialization of the general `update` image lemma; the only step is recognizing that identification.
Pi.single is Function.update applied to the zero function, so the image of the interval under single is the already-proved image-under-update statement specialized at 0. Pure specialization.

The weighted vector subtraction is defined as the base-point version at a fixed point, so restricting to the subset where weights are nonzero is exactly the already-proved statement for weightedVSubOfPoint; the proof is a direct specialization.

Weighted vector subtraction is defined as weightedVSubOfPoint at a fixed base point, so filtering out indices with zero weight is exactly the already-proved statement for weightedVSubOfPoint, specialised at that base point.

Dropping the zero-weight indices does not change the weighted vector subtraction, because weightedVSub is defined as weightedVSubOfPoint at a fixed base point and the corresponding statement is already proved there. A direct specialization.

Pure definitional unfolding: the bundled ring hom diagonalRingHom is defined with underlying function Matrix.diagonal, so applying its coercion is rfl. No mathematical step at all beyond unfolding the coercion.

Pure definitional unfolding: the bundled ring hom that sends a vector to its diagonal matrix is defined by that very formula, so applying its coercion reduces to the underlying function and the goal closes by rfl. No mathematical step at all.
Pure definitional unfolding: the bundled ring hom's underlying function is literally Matrix.diagonal, so the proof is rfl. No mathematical step at all.

A definitional-unfolding simp lemma: the ring equivalence built for an empty variable type computes, on application, to the stated formula (the constant/coefficient extraction) by rfl. All the algebraic-structure names are instance bookkeeping carried in the statement, not steps.

An API simp lemma stating what isEmptyRingEquiv does to an element; true by definitional unfolding of the equiv's forward map, closed by Eq.refl. The content is the definition of the equiv itself, not any argument.

A simp/API lemma stating what the isEmptyRingEquiv does on an element; it holds by definitional unfolding (Eq.refl). Everything else in the term is typeclass and coercion bookkeeping for the polynomial/AddMonoidAlgebra structures.

Definitional projection lemma: the object part of the extend-scalars pseudofunctor is by construction the stated module category, so unfolding the tower of pseudofunctor/prefunctor projections gives rfl. No mathematical step at all.
Reads off the object part of the extend-scalars pseudofunctor from its definition; true by rfl after peeling the Pseudofunctor -> PrelaxFunctor -> Prefunctor projections. No mathematics.
Computes the object part of the extend-scalars pseudofunctor; true by definition, so the proof is Eq.refl through the projection chain from Pseudofunctor down to Prefunctor.obj.

The constant polynomial 1 is C 1, so the Taylor shift fixes it: the proof is the constant-polynomial case of the Taylor lemma, with the numeral 1 identified definitionally with C 1 through the One/OfNat instance tower.
The constant polynomial 1 is C 1, so the Taylor shift fixes it; the proof is the taylor-of-a-constant lemma specialized at 1, with the rest instance projections for the numeral 1.

The polynomial 1 is the constant polynomial C 1, so the Taylor shift of it is itself by the constant-polynomial case; a one-step application of taylor_C, everything else is the numeral/one instance chain.
The left-multiplication dilation equivalence, applied to a point, is just multiplication; true by definitional unfolding of the coercion, proved by rfl.

The dilation equivalence given by left multiplication by a nonzero element evaluates to a * x; this holds by definition since mulLeft is built with that function as its toFun, so the proof is rfl. Pure unfolding of a coercion.
An 'apply' lemma: the underlying function of the dilation equivalence given by left multiplication by a nonzero element is left multiplication; true by definition, closed by rfl.
The identity map is conformal because it is conformal at every point; fix a point and cite the pointwise statement.

The identity map is conformal on the whole space because it is conformal at each point; the proof is the pointwise-to-global eta expansion, applying the ConformalAt version at an arbitrary point. No idea beyond quantifier introduction.
The identity map is conformal, which is just the pointwise statement conformalAt_id asserted at every point; no real content beyond unfolding Conformal as 'ConformalAt everywhere'.

Destructure the a.e.-measurability hypothesis into a measurable representative g together with f =ae g, note g is null-measurable, and transfer back along the (symmetrized) a.e. equality. The witness extraction is the real first step and no citation names it.

An a.e.-measurable function is null-measurable: destructure the AEMeasurable witness into a genuinely measurable g with f =ae g, note g is null-measurable, then transfer along the a.e. equality (with the direction of the equality flipped). The destructuring of the witness is a real step that no citation names.

Destructure the AEMeasurable hypothesis into a measurable representative g together with the a.e. equality f =ᵐ g; g is null measurable because measurable functions are, and null measurability transfers along the (reversed) a.e. equality. The witness extraction is the real first step and no citation names it.

Says that the coercion-to-function of the constant modular form is the constant function; true by definition of ModularForm.const, closed by rfl/Eq.refl. Content is unfolding a definition through the FunLike coercion, nothing else.
The coercion of the constant modular form is the constant function, true by definition; the proof is Eq.refl. Everything else is the ambient level-subgroup / weight typing needed to state it.

The coercion of the constant modular form to a function is the constant function, true by definition; the proof is Eq.refl after unfolding the FunLike coercion. All the group/matrix scaffolding is just the ambient setting.

Identifies trivializationAt of a vector bundle core with the local trivialization at the index of the base point, then applies the already-proved symmL formula for localTriv. Essentially a renaming of a known lemma through the FiberBundle interface.
The trivialization at a point is by definition the local trivialization at the index chosen for that point, so the statement is the already-proved localTriv_symmL specialized to indexAt x.

The trivialization at a point of a vector bundle core is by definition the local trivialization at the index of that point, so the statement reduces to the already-proved localTriv version of the symmL formula.

For p = infinity the eLpNorm is the essential sup, so the piecewise formula reduces immediately to the already-proved essential-sup piecewise lemma. The only step is that reduction plus citing one lemma.
At exponent infinity the eLpNorm is the essential sup, so the statement is the already-proved essential-sup formula for a piecewise function transported through that identification.
At exponent infinity the eLpNorm is the essential sup, so the statement is the already-proved essential-sup formula for a piecewise function, transported through that identification.
Lipschitz bound for the WithLp product coercion: the whole proof is a call to the private auxiliary lemma proved earlier in the file, under the Fact (1 <= p) hypothesis.

The coordinate map out of the L^p product space is Lipschitz for p >= 1; the entire argument lives in a private auxiliary lemma in the same file and this declaration just applies it. The Fact (1 <= p) instance is what supplies the exponent hypothesis.
The coordinate map out of the L^p product is Lipschitz with the stated constant; the whole argument is delegated verbatim to a private auxiliary lemma proved earlier in the file.

Two directions: given `a = b`, substitute to reduce to `Iff.rfl`; given `a ↔ b`, apply the axiom `propext`. The backward direction is where the real (axiomatic) content sits; the forward direction is a rewrite, and the `Eq.casesOn`/`HEq` material is just the elaborated substitution.
Two directions: right-to-left is exactly the axiom `propext`; left-to-right substitutes the equality of propositions (`▸`) and closes with `Iff.rfl`. Assembling those into an Iff is the rest.

Two directions. Forward: substitute along the equality of propositions and close with the reflexive iff. Backward: apply propositional extensionality, which is the axiom that makes the statement true. The Iff assembly plus the substitution is the rest.

Definitional: the locally-finite-order instance on a sum type is defined by cases on the two constructors, and the case of an interval from a right injection down to a left injection is defined to be the empty finset, so rfl closes it.

In the lexicographic-style order on a sum, an inr element is never below an inl element, and the LocallyFiniteOrder instance on Sum is defined so that this interval computes to the empty finset; hence `rfl`.

In the sum order no inl element is above an inr element, and the LocallyFiniteOrder instance on a sum is defined by cases so that this mixed open interval is literally the empty Finset. Proof is `rfl` — the content is that the instance computes definitionally.
Definitional: the composite equivalence is defined so that its underlying coalgebra hom is the composite of the underlying homs, so both sides are the same term and rfl closes it.
The underlying coalgebra hom of a composite coalgebra equivalence is by construction the composite of the underlying homs, so the proof is `rfl` unfolding `CoalgEquiv.trans`.

The underlying coalgebra hom of a composite coalgebra equivalence is the composite of the underlying homs; this is true by how CoalgEquiv.trans is defined, so the proof is `rfl`. Definitional, no citation carries the content.

This is the machine-generated reassociated form of functorMap_comp: take the composition identity, whisker it on the right by an arbitrary further morphism, and reassociate with the category associativity law. The mathematical content is entirely in functorMap_comp; the extra step is bookkeeping with assoc.

Auto-generated reassociated form of functorMap_comp: take the existing composition identity and whisker it on the right by an arbitrary further morphism, reassociating with the category associativity law. No new mathematics beyond the original lemma.

This is the mechanically reassociated form of functorMap_comp: take the existing composition identity, whisker it on the right by an arbitrary further morphism, and reassociate using the category associativity law.

Splits (p * X) iff Splits p: commute the two factors with mul_comm and cite the already-proved X * p version. The whole argument is commutativity plus one prior lemma, with simp-generated congruence residue around it.
Commute the product (p * X = X * p) and invoke the already-proved splits_X_mul; the only real content is commutativity of multiplication in the polynomial ring, the rest is simp closing an iff.
Splitting of p * X is the same as splitting of X * p, so commute the product and quote the already-proved X * p version; the rest is simp closing an iff by reflexivity.
Simp lemma naming the inverse functor of the self-duality equivalence of the category of Boolean algebras. Proved by rfl - it just projects a field out of the equivalence as constructed.
The inverse functor of the self-duality equivalence on Boolean algebras is by construction the stated functor, so the proof is rfl. Purely definitional.
Definitional: the inverse functor of the dual equivalence of Boolean algebras is by construction the stated functor, so the proof is rfl.
